transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That grey smelly water usually means something small has been left behind after a cycle, often because the drain path wasn't fully clear. Given your sink was replaced recently, there are two main possibilities: either food debris is catching in the dishwasher's own filter/pump area, or the connection at your new sink waste isn't allowing water to flow away freely (for example, if a blanking plug inside the spigot wasn't removed). Let's start with the easiest check. Please take out the lower rack, then twist and lift out the filter in the bottom of the tub. Rinse it under the tap and clear any food or grease from the sump underneath. Was the filter or sump blocked (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
I checked the filter and it was already clean, nothing blocking it. The dishwasher does drain fully at the end of a cycle, it's just that the dirty water seems to come back sometimes.

The issue is likely where the dishwasher empties into your new sink waste. If a blanking plug inside the sink spigot wasn't removed during installation, or if the sink trap is partially blocked, water will flow out during the cycle but then drain back in as the sink fills up later. Please check under the sink at that connection point and let me know if you found a blockage or a missing plug.

I had a look under the sink. Since the new sink went in, the drain hose just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, with no high loop in it. The sink also drains a little slowly. It seems to happen after I drain the sink of washing-up water.

The evidence points strongly to siphoning caused by the drain hose lying flat on the floor. Without a 'high loop' (where the hose goes up before dropping down into the sink waste), gravity can pull water back from the sink into the dishwasher whenever you run the tap or empty the sink. This explains why the water is smelly and grey—it's coming from your sink, not the machine itself. To fix this, please lift the drain hose so it arches up high (near the worktop level) before going down into the spigot. If you create that high loop and clear any slow drainage in the sink, the water should stop backing up.
Ok, I looped the hose up high and clipped it, and there's been no more water since. Is that all I need to do?

Yes, that is all you need to do. The high loop prevents the sink water from siphoning back into the machine, so your problem should be solved for good. Just keep an eye on that slow-draining sink trap occasionally; if it gets blocked again, the water level in the waste pipe will rise and could still cause a backup. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
